name: TextField
purpose: Let a user write or edit a single line of free text.
intent: Provide one consistent, accessible native text-input control - sizing, borders, and interaction states - that every free-text entry point in the product shares. Composes an optional leading icon/text slot and an optional trailing icon/action slot (which may itself compose a real Icon Button or Button), which is why it lives at the molecule tier rather than atom.

showCaret.note: Figma mockup-only, not a real prop.

placeholder.note: Figma mockup-only toggle between placeholder/value text, not a real prop.

elemBeforeInputComponent.note: Separate Figma component for the leading slot. Never interactive. The text case (e.g. a '$' currency prefix) is bound to fixed body-lg typography at every field size.

elemAfterInputComponent.note: Separate Figma component for the trailing slot. Frequently interactive (e.g. a clear action) - confirmed from a screenshot of the clear icon-button in its hover state. The icon-button case uses appearance=subtle, shape=square.

apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's 'state' axis (default/hover/focus/typing/filled) is not a real prop - verified from bound tokens: hover=:hover, focus=focused+empty (:focus-within + :placeholder-shown), typing=focused+has-value (:focus-within, not :placeholder-shown), filled=unfocused+has-value (not :placeholder-shown). All four derive from native pseudo-classes plus the input's own value; none are exposed as a prop.

Figma's 'tone' axis (standard/subtle) is renamed to 'appearance' (default/subtle) - a pure visual-weight distinction, matching this system's existing appearance vocabulary (see Button) rather than the semantic-meaning 'tone' word.
isInvalid renders with strokeWeight=2 even when not focused, confirmed directly from node data - invalid's thicker border is not a focus-only effect.

Figma's literal focus treatment thickens the frame's own border 1px->2px and swaps its color to --color-border-focused. Focus/typing replaces the resting border's color directly - the same pattern invalid already uses - rather than adding an outline ring around it, per explicit design feedback. Border width does not literally change to 2px, though: an earlier pass changed the real border-width on appearance=default's focus AND invalid, matching Figma directly, but that shifts the content box (and the placeholder/value text and typing caret) on every side, reported directly against the component from a side-by-side screenshot - both now paint the extra pixel via box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px <color> instead, keeping border-width a constant 1px in the box model with zero layout impact.

Hover is suppressed once the field is focused/typing (:focus-within, or the pinned data-force-state='focus' reference) - hover should only ever be visible on an inactive field, per explicit design feedback.

showCaret and placeholder (BOOLEAN) component properties exist only to drive Figma's own mockup and have no code equivalent - a real input shows its own caret and switches placeholder/value automatically.

appearance=subtle's bottom corners are always square (border-bottom-{left,right}-radius: 0), confirmed directly from Figma's per-corner radius data on the subtle variants - only the top corners share appearance=default's radius.

appearance=subtle rests at the same 1px bottom border-width appearance=default uses at rest, per explicit design feedback (an earlier pass reserved a constant 2px transparent border specifically to avoid a layout shift; that reservation was reverted). Reverting it reintroduced the shift a real border-width change causes (the vertically-centered text visibly nudges by a pixel), so focus/invalid on appearance=subtle now paint the thicker look via box-shadow (inset 0 -1px 0 0 <color>) instead, keeping border-bottom-width a constant 1px in the box model at every state - zero layout impact. appearance.default's own invalid/focus still uses a real border-width change (a whole-box change on all four sides is a much smaller relative shift there), so this technique is specific to appearance=subtle.

`.root[data-invalid='true']` sets the border-width shorthand (all four sides) to 2px; `.appearance_subtle[data-invalid='true']` overrides border-top/right/left-width back to 0 and must also explicitly reset border-bottom-width back to 1px, or that side silently inherits the shorthand's leftover 2px and reintroduces the same text shift.

Hovering an invalid appearance=subtle field keeps the error border color rather than resetting to --color-border-input, per explicit design feedback - the border-color-changing hover rule is scoped with :not([data-invalid='true']); the background-changing hover rule is not, since hover should still tint the background on an invalid field.

elemBeforeInput and elemAfterInput are separate, asymmetric Figma components (icon|text vs icon-button|button), not a symmetric before/after pair - iconBefore is always aria-hidden, iconAfter is never forced aria-hidden.
Inline padding is asymmetric per size (tighter on the end side) and the icon/input gap varies per size (4px/6px/8px) rather than a flat 6px, confirmed directly from Figma's per-side bound variables.

antiPatterns: choosing from a fixed set of options
faking an input with a non-form element

anatomy.description: Bordered frame holding the optional before/action slots and the input; reacts to :hover and :focus-within.
Optional leading icon or short text prefix. Always decorative - never interactive.
The real native text input; carries all forwarded native attributes.
Optional trailing icon or interactive action (e.g. an IconButton clear button). Never forced aria-hidden.

size.description: Frame height, padding, gap, and typography.

appearance.description: default is bordered at rest, rounded on all four corners; subtle has no visible border/background until hover, focus, or invalid, and always has square bottom corners.

invalid.description: Sets aria-invalid and the error border (thicker, regardless of focus).

iconBefore.description: Optional leading icon or short text prefix. Always decorative (aria-hidden).

iconAfter.description: Optional trailing icon or interactive control (typically an IconButton clear action, or a Button). Never forced aria-hidden.

className.description: Composes with the root frame's class list.

inputClassName.description: Composes with the native input's class list.

default.purpose: Bordered box with a raised-surface background at rest, rounded on all four corners.

subtle.purpose: No visible border/background until hover, focus, or invalid; bottom corners always square regardless of size.

slots.name: iconBefore
supports: a small icon from the generated icon set

slots.name: iconAfter
supports: a small icon from the generated icon set
an IconButton (appearance=subtle, shape=square) for a clear/dismiss action
a Button for a labeled action

requirements: Render a real native <input> - never fake one.
Set aria-invalid on the input when invalid is true.
iconBefore is aria-hidden - decorative only, never interactive.
iconAfter is never forced aria-hidden - it may hold a real interactive control (e.g. an IconButton clear action) which must keep its own accessible name and stay keyboard-reachable.
Text Field does not manage labelling - pair with a native label[htmlFor] or aria-label/aria-labelledby.

keyboardInteraction: Native input keyboard behavior - Tab to focus, type to enter text.
When iconAfter holds an interactive control, Tab reaches it as its own stop after the input, in native DOM order.
behaviorRules: Render a real <input> inside a bordered frame div.
hover/focus/typing/filled are never props - they derive from :hover, :focus-within, and :placeholder-shown plus the input's own value.
invalid always renders the thicker error border regardless of focus state.

The focused-frame indicator replaces the resting border color directly (:focus-within), the same pattern invalid uses, not an outline ring around it. Border-width stays a constant 1px on appearance=default at every state (rest, hover, focus, invalid) - focus/invalid instead paint a thicker look via box-shadow, so the text/caret never shifts horizontally.
Hover is suppressed while the field is focused/typing (:focus-within), on both appearances.
appearance=subtle always renders square bottom corners (0 radius), regardless of size.
appearance=subtle rests at 1px border-width, the same as appearance=default, at every state - focus/invalid look thicker via box-shadow only, never a real border-bottom-width change.
Hover never overrides the invalid border color on appearance=subtle - only the background changes on hover when invalid is also true.
iconBefore is icon-or-text only, always aria-hidden; iconAfter is icon-or-action, never forced aria-hidden.
compositionRules: Pair with a native label[htmlFor] or aria-label/aria-labelledby - Text Field does not include one.
Use Select instead of Text Field when the value comes from a fixed set of options.
For an interactive iconAfter clear/dismiss action, use a real IconButton (appearance=subtle, shape=square) rather than a bare icon standing in for a button.
contentRules: Single line only - no textarea mode.
Content should match the native `type` in use.
themeRules: Must work in light and dark themes - all colors use semantic tokens.
implementationNotes: Use React.memo + React.forwardRef<HTMLInputElement> for the exported component.
No hardcoded colors, spacing, radius, or typography, except the documented --measurement-6 gap (matches Toggle Button's own precedent for the same missing spacing/075 token).
Do not add a state prop - hover/focus/typing/filled are all native pseudo-class/value-driven.
do: Use the native type attribute (email, password, search, ...) for the right keyboard and built-in validation.
Pair with a native label[htmlFor] pointing at the input's id.
Use appearance=subtle for a search box or inline-edit field that shouldn't visually compete with surrounding content until interacted with.
Use a real IconButton (appearance=subtle, shape=square) for an interactive iconAfter clear/dismiss action.
dont: Do not use for multi-line content.
Do not use for a value chosen from a fixed set of options.
Do not fake an input with a styled non-form element.
Do not force aria-hidden on an interactive iconAfter control.
acceptanceCriteria: Supports all TextFieldSize and TextFieldAppearance values.
invalid sets aria-invalid=true and the thicker error border, regardless of focus.
disabled prevents interaction and applies disabled tokens.
appearance=subtle renders square bottom corners at every size.
appearance=subtle rests at the same 1px border-width as appearance=default.
Hovering an invalid appearance=subtle field keeps the error border color visible.
iconBefore renders as decorative (aria-hidden); iconAfter renders without a forced aria-hidden and stays focusable when it holds a real IconButton/Button.
Placeholder vs. value text color follows :placeholder-shown automatically, with no state prop.
Focus/typing replaces the resting border color/width via :focus-within, the same way invalid does.
Hover never shows while the field is focused/typing.
Works in light and dark themes.
Storybook includes Playground, Variants, States, Content, and Edge Cases.
Tests cover rendering, size/appearance, invalid, disabled, icons, interactive iconAfter accessibility, and native attribute forwarding.
knownLimitations: No integrated label, helper text, or error message - Figma's source component doesn't include them.
--measurement-6 (Figma's spacing/075) has no semantic spacing token yet.
futureEnhancements: A 'Form Field' molecule composing a label, this input, and helper/error text
A textarea variant if a real multi-line use case emerges
